rounds.hypothesis: diagnose's root cause holds as written: the only IPC permission gate is the stub IpcNamespace::validate_sem_set, so IPC_STAT on a mode-0 set returns 0 instead of EACCES. Filling in the stub alone would turn the test green, but it would also convert every *wrong* PermissionMode still passed by a sibling call site from a harmless no-op into a wrong denial. So the round is: implement the predicate on the shared IpcPermission type, and simultaneously correct every request that reaches it.
rounds.change: Added IpcPermission::check_access (kernel/src/ipc/mod.rs), mirroring Linux ipcperms(): exclusive owner/group/other triplet selection on EUID vs uid/cuid then in_group_p on gid/cguid, denial when requested & !granted & 0o7 != 0, with a CAP_IPC_OWNER escape whose EPERM is swallowed into EACCES. Moved PermissionMode up from ipc/semaphore/system_v to ipc/ beside IpcPermission and gave it from_mode() for Linux's (m>>6)|(m>>3)|m fold. De-stubbed validate_sem_set to delegate; threaded &PosixThread through with_sem_set (6 semctl.rs sites, 1 sem.rs site) and get_or_create_sem_set. Corrected two wrong requests: semop now asks ALTER or READ off its existing is_alter instead of empty(), and the semget lookup folds the caller's own mode instead of hardcoding ALTER|READ. Moved the semget permission check after the EEXIST and nsems checks to match ipcget_public() ordering. Added with_sem_set_unchecked for semop's post-wakeup withdrawal, which is re-entry on an already-authorized access.
rounds.outcome: green on round 1: 'All conformance tests passed.', 1 passed / 0 failed / 0 broken / 0 skipped / 0 warnings, and the target line 'semctl02.c:26: TPASS: semctl(IPC_STAT) with nobody user : EACCES (13)'. Re-run once more against the final tree after reverting the KIRK_VERBOSE edit; still green.

rounds.hypothesis: Not a failure round. semctl02's set has mode 0, so every triplet of it is 0 and the test cannot discriminate triplet selection -- as diagnose's notes warned, a fix that ORed the triplets or fell through to the group branch would also pass it. Spent the second boot buying that discrimination from tests rather than trusting one assertion.
rounds.change: One extra boot with CONFORMANCE_TEST_SELECTOR=semctl02,semctl07,semget01,semget02,semop03 and KIRK_VERBOSE forced on, to read every per-case line: the three enabled regression risks named by diagnose, plus semget02 as a cross-check because its case 1 is nobody vs root's 0600 set, i.e. the *other* triplet denial that semctl02 never exercises.
rounds.outcome: 34 passed / 0 failed / 0 broken / 0 skipped / 0 warnings across all five. semctl07's 16 root-path assertions, semget01 and semop03 all still green, so no regression. All six semget02 cases pass, which pins three things semctl02 cannot: 'semget(key,10,384) : EACCES' is the other-triplet denial through the new fold, 'semget(key,10,1536) : EEXIST' confirms EEXIST still precedes the permission check, and 'semget(key,11,384) : EINVAL' confirms the nsems check does too. The KIRK_VERBOSE edit was reverted afterwards and is not in patch.diff.

layer: Matches diagnose's owning_layer: the shared SysV IPC permission layer. The predicate is a method on IpcPermission in kernel/src/ipc/mod.rs, the type that already stores key/uid/gid/cuid/cguid/mode and nothing semaphore-specific, and it is invoked from IpcNamespace where the stub sat. It is deliberately not in SemaphoreSet and not open-coded in the sys_sem* handlers: the rule is byte-identical for message queues and shared memory, which ipc_ns.rs's own module doc says 'remain to be added', so msgctl/shmctl will inherit one function instead of re-deriving it. PermissionMode moved up out of semaphore/system_v for the same reason -- leaving it there would have made the shared layer depend on the semaphore submodule, exactly backwards for msg/shm reuse. The whole rule including the CAP_IPC_OWNER escape lives in that one function rather than being split with the escape in IpcNamespace, so a future caller cannot get the mode test but forget the capability.
generalizes:
This is the opposite of narrow: the stub was the only permission gate in all of SysV IPC, so one predicate fixes every caller at once. All six semctl commands that already passed a meaningful mode were unchecked -- IPC_STAT, SEM_GETPID, SEM_GETVAL, SEM_GETNCNT, SEM_GETZCNT (READ) and SEM_SETVAL (ALTER) -- meaning any process could read or overwrite any semaphore set in the namespace; all six are now checked with no call-site change. Nothing branches on the flag, size or errno semctl02 supplies: the code path for IPC_STAT is the shared with_sem_set path, and mode 0 is not special-cased anywhere.

Two call sites had to be corrected precisely *because* a real predicate generalizes. sys_semop passed PermissionMode::empty() with a TODO, so a live gate would have authorized nothing there; it now asks ALTER or READ off the is_alter it already computed, matching Linux's alter ? S_IWUGO : S_IRUGO, which closes semop's hole rather than leaving it. The semget lookup hardcoded ALTER|READ; had I filled in the stub and left that, a non-root caller opening an existing 0644 set read-only would have started getting EACCES where Linux returns the id -- a denial my own change would have introduced. Folding the caller's mode the way Linux does makes it strictly more faithful, and semget02's six passing cases exercise it. Reordering the semget check after EEXIST/EINVAL is the same kind of correction: with a live gate, a non-root caller doing IPC_CREAT|IPC_EXCL on an inaccessible set would otherwise get EACCES where Linux gives EEXIST. No test in the suite covers that input, which is why it is called out here rather than resting on green.

The triplet rule is verified beyond the one assertion, since semctl02's mode-0 set makes all three triplets identical and cannot tell them apart: semget02 case 1 (nobody vs root's 0600 set, EACCES) exercises the other branch, and diagnose's host probes pin the rest -- mode 077 denies its owner both ways, so selection is exclusive rather than a union, which is why the code is an if / else if / else chain and not an OR of triplets. Root keeps working through CAP_IPC_OWNER, not through a bypass: credentials_.rs gives root CapSet::all(), and set_resuid_unchecked drops it on the root->nobody transition, so nobody is judged by the mode as it must be.

Two things left deliberately unchanged, both pre-existing and both in the permissive direction, so neither is a hole this patch opens. IPC_RMID still hand-rolls euid == uid || euid == cuid and still lacks CAP_SYS_ADMIN; that is Linux's separate ipcctl_obtain_check rule, it must stay off the mode-based path or semctl02's own cleanup on a mode-0 set would break, and it is outside this invariant, which is scoped to operations other than removal and ownership change. Creation stays unchecked, matching ipcget_new. PermissionMode::EXEC was added so from_mode() never silently drops a user-supplied execute bit, even though no IPC operation requests it.
fix_summary:
Turns the SysV IPC permission stub into a real check at the shared layer, and corrects every request that now reaches it.

IpcPermission::check_access is the whole of Linux's ipcperms() in one function: it selects exactly one triplet of the object's mode from the caller's credentials -- owner when EUID matches uid or cuid, else group when the object's gid or cguid is in the caller's groups, else other -- and denies with EACCES when the requested access is not a subset of it. Selection is exclusive, so an object whose mode is 0 denies its own owner, which is the rule semctl02 turns on. CAP_IPC_OWNER exempts the caller, and because lsm_hooks::on_capable reports a missing capability as EPERM, its error is swallowed and converted to EACCES -- propagating it would have made the test fail with the wrong errno while looking like a working check.

The Asterinas abstractions it is designed against, and why: (1) IpcPermission rather than SemaphoreSet, because the type is already IPC-generic and the rule is identical for the msg/shm implementations that ipc_ns.rs says are still to come. (2) PermissionMode, moved up beside IpcPermission, as the request type -- it was already in Linux's folded low-three-bit form, so it needed no redesign, only a from_mode() fold and relocation so the shared layer does not reach down into the semaphore submodule. (3) lsm_hooks::on_capable with the namespace-scoped CapableContext for the capability escape, the same hook IpcNamespace already uses for CAP_SYS_ADMIN, rather than reading a capset directly. (4) Explicit &PosixThread threaded through with_sem_set instead of Asterinas's other precedent for permission checks, Inode::check_permission, which reads Task::current() and fails open when there is no current thread; the argument is one line per call site and cannot fail open. Its counterpart with_sem_set_unchecked, scoped pub(in crate::ipc), names the one genuinely unauthorized re-entry -- semop withdrawing its own pending operation after wakeup, which Linux likewise does not re-check -- so that 'no permission required' is stated rather than encoded as an empty request.

Group membership follows Linux's in_group_p, which tests FSGID plus supplementary groups rather than EGID; the helper is commented to that effect since the asymmetry with the EUID-based owner test looks like a bug otherwise.
